intent: Single-variable test against iteration 5: narrow wheel_track from 0.10 m to 0.09 m, keeping the iteration 5 sensor layout, radius 0.040 m and mass 0.5 kg. This adds turn authority for the s-bend, where max_error is pinned at the off-track limit, while leaving the sensing that has already been tuned unchanged.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Track 0.09 m raises s-bend progress above 0.72 and lowers s-bend max_error below 0.06 m, because turn rate per wheel-speed difference rises about 11%. (2) Oval finish rate stays at or above 90%. (3) If steering_oscillation rises sharply while max_error does not move, the limit is controller gain, not turn authority, and the Integrator should retune kp/kd. (4) If slalom line_loss_events stay near 1.85 with no change in slalom progress, the slalom limit is sensor coverage, so the next step is outer sensors at about ±0.045 m with the 16 mm footprint. (5) If the s-bend stays at 0.06 m with few line losses, the next step is to revisit the forward offset, not mass.
rationale: Evidence from the development results. Iteration 5 (mass 0.5 kg, 5 sensors at y=0.07 m, 16 mm footprint, track 0.10 m, radius 0.040 m) scored 422.9. Iteration 6 cut mass to 0.4 kg and scored 422.1. The oval finish rate held at 95%, but s-bend progress fell from 0.72 to 0.59 and s-bend finishes dropped to 2 of 20 (on 0.4 kg the s-bend got worse, not better). Mass is therefore no longer the lever, and 0.5 kg is the better operating point. Two bottlenecks remain. (1) On the s-bend, max_error sits at the 0.06 m off-track limit with about 1.1 line-loss events, which points to turn authority rather than sensing. (2) On the slalom, progress is about 0.14 and line losses are 1.85, which points to sensor coverage on alternating bends. The sensor layout has been tested in several forms, and the 5-sensor, y=0.07 m, 16 mm layout remains the best-supported. I therefore keep the sensors fixed and test one change against iteration 5: the wheel track, narrowed from 0.10 m to 0.09 m. Physically, yaw rate equals the wheel-speed difference divided by the track, so a narrower track gives about 11% more yaw rate for the same wheel-speed difference. The controller's turn command is unchanged, so this only adds turn authority on tight bends. Mass returns to 0.5 kg, the iteration 5 value, which had the better s-bend mean progress. Expected result: s-bend progress rises above 0.72 with fewer line-loss events and max_error below 0.06 m, and the oval finish rate stays at or above 90%. The risk is more steering oscillation on the oval, since higher turn rate can overshoot.
